subject: Recap: First call — migration strategy off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Katherine Miles <k.miles@wellpath.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: First call — migration strategy off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Katherine —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points you shared
- Monthly API spend with current providers (OpenAI + Anthropic) has grown to ~$62k; cost predictability is primary driver.
- Vendor lock-in: model behavior and tooling are tied to hosted APIs; difficulty porting prompt engineering and function/tool calls.
- Latency and throughput: customer-facing chat has 95th percentile latency spikes during peak that impact SLAs.
- Compliance: need for VPC/private deployment option and audit logs for PHI-handling flows.

Current stack (from the call)
- Production: OpenAI (gpt-4o for high-accuracy tasks, gpt-3.5 for bulk assistants).
- Experiments: Anthropic Claude-2 for few-shot summarization.
- Orchestration: home-grown router that fans out calls; caching is ad-hoc via Redis.

Success criteria (what counts as a win)
- <=40% reduction in unit inference cost for high-volume assistant flows (token-level) without more than 5% drop in end-user satisfaction metrics.
- 95th pctl latency at or below current baseline for interactive chat (goal: <600ms).
- Private deployment option (VPC with customer-managed keys) and SOC 2 evidence for procurement.

Initial compatibility notes we discussed
- Need parity for streaming responses and tool/function calling.
- Must support current prompt templates and tokenization patterns; minimizing behavioral drift is important.
- Embeddings: migrate without rebuild of downstream search if possible (same dimensionality preferred).

Proposed short shortlist of open model candidates (high-level) — we will validate with benchmarking in next step:
- Llama 3 8B (quant-friendly, good instruction-following after finetune)
- Mistral Instruct variant (strong cost/perf for instruction tasks)
- Red-Open-1-mini (our internal Redwood-curated 4-bit profile for low latency)

Immediate next steps
1) I will share a migration checklist and preliminary SOW draft (attached).
2) We propose a technical deep-dive with your infra lead + our infra eng to map the routing/telemetry integration — availability: Wed/Thu next week.
3) Redwood will run a short A/B pilot on a non-critical assistant to measure latency/cost and user regressions (2–3 weeks).

Attachments: redwood-migration-checklist.xlsx, SOW-draft-Redwood-WellPath-v1.docx

If the above looks right, can we lock in 60–90 minutes for the technical deep-dive on Wed 5/27 or Thu 5/28? I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D +1 (415) 555-0192 | dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
redwood.ai

From: Katherine Miles <k.miles@wellpath.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: WellPath AI Procurement <procurement@wellpath.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap: First call — migration strategy off proprietary LLM APIs

Thanks Dylan — this recap is accurate and helpful. A few clarifications / data points from my side: 

- Spend breakout: OpenAI ~ $48k/mo (assistant + embeddings), Anthropic ~ $14k/mo (experiments).
- Latency SLA: our contractual target for chat is 95th pctl <750ms; typical baseline now is ~700ms but spikes to 1.2s during traffic bursts.
- Embeddings usage: vector size is 1536 (we use a vector DB hosted in our VPC). Ideally we avoid a reindex if possible.
- Security Q: I attached our initial security questionnaire (WellPath_Security_Q.pdf) — can you confirm data isolation and audit log availability for the private deployment?

Procurement timeline: we are aiming to select a vendor and start an initial pilot by end of June. Legal will want SOC 2 Type II and an option to run on our VPC.

Model behavior note: our internal product team is sensitive to any change in summarization tone — a 10–15% drop in NPS for the assistant is a hard stop.

Confirming we can do Thu 5/28 for the deep-dive (afternoon PT). Please send invite.

— Katherine
Katherine Miles
Head of Product, AI — WellPath AI
k.miles@wellpath.ai | +1 212-555-0123

Attachment: WellPath_Security_Q.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Katherine Miles <k.miles@wellpath.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, WellPath AI Procurement <procurement@wellpath.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: First call — migration strategy off proprietary LLM APIs

Appreciate the details, Katherine — they help a lot. Short responses inline and then a proposed plan for the deep-dive.

- Spend & embeddings: noted on 1536 vector size; we’ll prioritize model variants that provide compatible embedding dims or document a minimal reindex path.
- Security: Redwood Private supports VPC deployment with customer-managed KMS, and we can expose audit logs (immutable event stream) for the pilot. I’ll attach our SOC 2 letter and a short compliance one-pager in the follow-up.
- Tone/satisfaction: pilot design will include an A/B evaluation harness against your current endpoints and critical prompt sets (we’ll measure NPS + task success to ensure regressions <5%).

Model shortlist rationale (more detail)
- Llama 3 8B: good instruction-following after light RLHF/finetune; expected cost reduction ~35% on our bench for conversational tasks.
- Mistral Instruct: top-tier instruction quality for medium budgets; we expect cost parity with Llama 3 but often stronger in summarization.
- Redwood-1-mini (quantized): engineered for sub-300ms latency at 1–2 token/window use-cases; excellent for lower-cost bulk assistants.

Proposed next steps (to be covered on Thu 5/28 deep-dive)
1) Infra mapping: how your router and Redis caching will integrate with Redwood runtime and where we can place KV prefix caches. (Engineering owners: your infra lead + our runtime eng).
2) Pilot plan: success metrics, traffic shaping, sampling rates, rollback/fallback to current endpoints.
3) Security & procurement: SOC 2 evidence, SOC letter, and draft contract milestones.
4) Timeline & SOW: confirm pilot start date (target the week of 6/8) and milestones for production rollout.

I’ve attached the migration checklist and SOW draft again. I’ll also upload the SOC letter to the Drive link and post the HubSpot record here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/98765

Confirming Thu 2026-05-28 14:00 PT / 17:00 ET works for us. I’ll send calendar invite with dial-in + agenda.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-migration-checklist.xlsx, SOW-draft-Redwood-WellPath-v1.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Recap: First call — migration strategy off proprietary LLM APIs

Dylan — quick internal note before you send the invite to Katherine: procurement sensitivity on price. If they want ~40% unit-cost reduction we should be prepared to offer a structured pilot discount and a 12–18 month committed plan to hit the numbers. Recommend:

- Pilot: 50% off inference unit rates for the 2–3 week pilot (cap at $8k).
- If pilot meets success criteria, commit to a 12-month Dedicated/Hosted blended contract with a step-down schedule (start at 20% off list, move to 30% after 3 months).

Also loop Alex Martinez from Pricing if legal needs redlines on the SOW. I added redwood-migration-checklist.xlsx notes on telemetry hooks we should capture during pilot.

Cc’ing you on the changes that I made to the SOW draft. Send the invite and include the pilot discount proposal as a slide in the deck for Thu’s deep-dive.

— Marissa
